statement: A singly linked list is a chain of nodes. Each node stores one value and a next pointer to the node after it; the last node, the tail, points to null.
You are given an array values. Build a singly linked list that holds these values in the same order: create one node per value and link each node to the next one.
Return the head of the new list. The examples show the value stored in the head node.

examples.explanation: The head holds 4. Following next pointers from it visits 8, 15 and 16, and the tail, 16, points to null.
The head holds 2, then 7, then the tail 1, whose next pointer is null.
